label: The king
summary: In theory the sole officiant in every temple and the guarantor of maat. In practice priests acted as delegates while temple reliefs kept showing the king making the offering.

relations.note: The living king is Horus; the dead king is assimilated to Osiris.

label: Hem-netjer, god's servant
summary: The senior priestly rank permitted to approach the cult image. Many posts were part-time, rotating, and tied to income from temple estates.

label: Wab priest
summary: A lower-ranking purified servant who carried, cleaned, and provisioned but did not normally face the god directly.

label: Lector priest
aliases: he who carries the ritual book
summary: The reader of the ritual book, whose recitation made the rite effective. Later stories make the lector priest the figure who performs wonders.

label: Temple singer and musician
summary: Women and men who sang, shook the sistrum, and pacified the god. The title of chantress of Amun became common for elite Theban women.

label: Tomb artisan
summary: The workers who cut and decorated royal tombs. Their village at Deir el-Medina supplies most of what is known about ordinary religious life in the New Kingdom.

label: Cultivator
summary: Most Egyptians. Their year followed inundation, sowing, and harvest, and their religious record survives mainly through institutions that taxed and employed them.

label: Embalmer
summary: Specialists who prepared the body in the embalming place, working under Anubis's patronage and within a trade whose prices and grades are partly documented.
